questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to combine deque operations with real-time median maintenance, including duplicates and lazy deletions, under amortized log-time guarantees.

## Key Concepts
- Median maintenance with two multisets/heaps
- Lazy deletion to handle arbitrary pops from either end
- Balancing invariants to retrieve lower median for even sizes

## Code Example
```pseudo
class MedianDeque:
  left: Multiset // max-heap behavior
  right: Multiset // min-heap behavior
  delLeft, delRight: Map

  pushFront(x): insert into left; rebalance
  pushBack(x): insert into right; rebalance
  popFront(): mark in delLeft; prune; rebalance
  popBack(): mark in delRight; prune; rebalance
  median(): return max(left) if |left| > |right| else max(left)
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend this for a sliding window median over a fixed-size window?
- What are the memory implications of lazy deletions and how would you bound them over time?

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked
- Real-world systems track overlapping time/space intervals (e.g., CDN rules, query routing) and need fast point queries and k-th weight selections across overlaps.

Key Concepts
- Coordinate compression, segment tree on the line.
- Each interval maps to O(log n) nodes; per-node multisets track weights.
- Sum at a point aggregates per-node totals; k-th uses cross-node rank aggregation via binary search over weights.

Code Example
```javascript
class Node { constructor() { this.weights = new Map(); this.total = 0; } add(w){ this.weights.set(w,(this.weights.get(w)||0)+1); this.total+=w; } remove(w){ const c=this.weights.get(w)||0; if(c<=1) this.weights.delete(w); else this.weights.set(w,c-1); this.total-=w; } }
```

Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle dynamic coordinate ranges with inserts at new coordinates without rebuilding?
- What are potential optimizations for the kthLargestWeightAtPoint when weight domain is small or large?

Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a time-ordered data structure with dynamic updates and range Kadane queries, useful for analytics with streaming events.

Key Concepts

- Kadane’s algorithm generalized to segments via a monoid: sum, pref, suff, best.
- Handling duplicates by aggregating per timestamp.
- Range queries using split/merge or traversal to collect O(log n) aggregates.

Code Example

```javascript
function combine(left, right){ /* merge Kadane aggregates */ }
```
